title: Lock Poisoning and Invariants
body: Every RwLock and Mutex in this binary guards something the orchestrator is the sole author of — the shell layout, the pty table, the resolved stack, the open project. A poisoned lock means an earlier thread panicked partway through a write, so the value behind it is half-applied. Stopping at the first access is better than serving a half-applied state. STANDARDS.md section 5 allows the panic — a mutex you own is its own example of a genuine invariant — and asks for a comment naming the invariant.
